name: Mount Tom White
generated_description:
At 11,211 feet, Mount Tom White is a summit in Alaska. With roughly 7,641 feet of topographic prominence, it stands well above the surrounding terrain.

When to Go

The reliable snow-free window is roughly July through September. At this elevation, afternoon thunderstorms are a serious summer hazard — start early and plan to be off the upper mountain by midday. Outside that window expect snow travel and bring traction and navigation skills to match.

Know Before You Go

Download the GPX track from this page before you go — cell coverage is unreliable in the mountains and a saved route works offline in any GPS app. Conditions change: verify current access, closures and weather with the official land manager before you go.
